_comment: Declarative disk-full defense. Source of truth for: per-mount watch thresholds, systemd-tmpfiles cleanup rules, journald limits, docker retention, and reclaim actions. Nix module `configuration_system-protection.nix` reads this file and generates systemd units + tmpfiles.d + logrotate rules. Change what gets protected = edit this file, `build.sh ship` home-manager.

emergency._comment: HARD stop-the-bleeding tier, ABOVE every per-mount critical. When ANY watched mount hits `pct`, the watchdog runs `actions` IN ORDER: (1) emergency_signal — VERBOSE journal explanation (journalctl -t disk-emergency), urgent ntfy, and a wall broadcast to every terminal, so the cause is unmissable; (2) kill_nonsystem — SIGTERM every process in `kill_slices` (the non-system background tier) to stop the bleeders writing; (3) freeze_nonsystem — cgroup-v2 FREEZE of `freeze_slices` so any survivor's writes HALT instantly (paused, not killed — no data loss) while we clean; (4) the reclaim actions; (5) thaw_nonsystem — un-freeze. `protected_slices` (os-essentials = ssh/wg/session/the watchdog itself) is NEVER killed or frozen, so the box stays reachable. Defaults are conservative — they target workload.slice (background), not the live desktop session; widen freeze_slices/kill_slices here (data-driven, no code change) for more aggression.

watches._comment: Per-mount threshold-triggered actions. `critical_pct` fires the action list. Actions defined in `actions` map below.

mounts.description: tmpfs root — NixOS impermanence; filling blocks login, breaks systemd
btrfs user data — slow-fill; primary dev workspace
btrfs @shared — persistent app state, audit logs, configs
Nix store — only shrinks via gc
p5 ext4 — Docker data-root + the dev-store chroot Nix store (~25G dev toolchain off the pool)

tmpfiles_rules._comment: Written to /etc/tmpfiles.d/50-cloud-data-disk-protection.conf via nix module. Format: `d <path> - - - <age> -`. Age in d (days), h (hours), m (minutes).
tmpfiles_rules._comment_dev-store: The last rule PROVISIONS (not cleans) a diego-owned DEV-STORE root on /mnt/shared-lib (p5, ~83G free) — a chroot Nix store (storeDir=/nix/store) holding the heavy dev toolchain (~25G) OFF the 80G pool. /mnt/shared-lib is root-owned ext4 so the user-tier home-manager cannot create it; the NixOS host does, here. Populated by bc_flakes_dev-store/build.sh, entered via the `dev` bwrap shell. Supersedes the 2026-06-18 android-only dirs — android-emulator is now a normal dev leaf inside this store. Plan: 0_tasks/PLAN_dev-store-split.md.

tmp_mounts._comment: Dedicated /tmp (btrfs, persistent, 3d age) + /tmpfs (RAM, ephemeral, 1d age). Decouples scratch from the 2G impermanence root so a leaky script can no longer block login by filling /. Nix module `configuration_tmp.nix` reads this and generates fileSystems.* + tmpfiles D! rules + activation-script that creates missing btrfs subvolumes. Rationale: previously /tmp lived inside tmpfs root and routinely hit 97% from orphaned working copies (e.g. /tmp/cloud-clean-work).

mounts.description: Large persistent scratch — wiped on boot, age 3 days. Use for build dirs, git worktrees, anything that might grow.
Fast RAM-backed scratch — 2G cap, wiped on every boot (tmpfs is RAM). Use for quick cache, ipc, workloads that benefit from RAM speed.

journald_limits._comment: systemd-journald.conf values — data-driven. Applied via nix module `services.journald.extraConfig`.

docker_retention._comment: Weekly `docker system prune` guarded by free-space check. Only prunes when real disk is >75% full to avoid churning healthy state.

cargo_sweep._comment: cargo-sweep keeps ~/.cargo/target/ bounded. Runs weekly; keeps only targets touched in last `keep_days`.

nix_gc._comment: Nix store garbage collection. Keeps generations younger than `keep_days`.

script_hygiene._comment: CI lint rules for scripts that create tmp dirs. Each violation fails CI.

actions._comment: Action definitions. Nix module generates the corresponding ExecStart for disk-watchdog.service.

purge_tmp_worktrees.description: Remove orphaned worktree dirs under /tmp (no active process)

purge_audit_old.description: Delete /mnt/shared/log/audit/* older than 3 days (auditd rotation backstop)

docker_prune_volumes_dangling.description: Prune dangling docker volumes — NEVER named volumes

dev_store_gc.description: GC the p5 dev-store chroot Nix store (keeps the current profile gcroot)

emergency_signal.description: VERBOSE journal (logger -t disk-emergency -p user.alert) + urgent ntfy + wall broadcast — explains which mount is full, the %, and exactly what the watchdog is about to do. The unmissable 'disk is full, writes are being stopped for cleanup' signal.

kill_nonsystem.description: SIGTERM every process in emergency.kill_slices (non-system background tier). Stops the bleeders writing. os-essentials.slice is never targeted.

freeze_nonsystem.description: cgroup-v2 freeze of emergency.freeze_slices — survivors' writes halt instantly (paused, reversible, no data loss) while reclaim runs.

thaw_nonsystem.description: Un-freeze emergency.freeze_slices after reclaim. Always runs last so a transient spike never leaves the slice frozen.

testers._comment: Each tester verifies one invariant of the disk defense. Wire into reports-logs or a dedicated CI job.

checks.description: disk-watchdog.service is active on all VMs + desktop
/tmp is its own btrfs mount (not inside tmpfs root)
/tmpfs is its own tmpfs RAM mount
systemd-tmpfiles has D! /tmp rule (wipe on boot)
systemd-tmpfiles has D! /tmpfs rule (age + wipe on boot)
Root tmpfs usage < 50% (since /tmp is no longer on it)
auditd writes to /mnt/shared (btrfs), not /var/log/audit on tmpfs
tmpfiles has e rule that ages /mnt/shared/log/audit at 3d
/ watch's critical action list includes purge_audit_old
os-essentials.slice (ssh/wg/session/watchdog) is NEVER killed or frozen
emergency action list starts with the signal and ends with the thaw (so a spike never leaves a slice frozen)
no protected slice is also a freeze/kill target (never freeze ssh/session)

deployment.deploy_to_vms_command: for vm in gcp-proxy gcp-t4 oci-mail oci-analytics oci-apps; do (cd ~/git/cloud/b_infra/nixhm-sudo-$vm && ./build.sh ship); done
